messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Esperanto, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Esperanto line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|----------------------|--------------------|-----------------------|--------| | **ché** | causal conjunction “because” | **ĉar** | because | OK | | **questa** | demonstrative adjective “this” (modifies *bestia*) | **ĉi tiu** | this | OK | | **bestia** | noun “beast” (subject) | **bestio** | beast | OK | | **per** | preposition introducing relative clause “for which” | **pro** | because of / for which | OK | | **la** | definite article (feminine) – part of *la qual* | — | (none) | **UNNECESSARY** | | **qual** | relative pronoun “which” (refers to *bestia*) | **kiu** | which | OK | | **tu** | 2nd‑person pronoun “you” (subject of *gride*) | **vi** | you | OK | | **gride** | verb “cries out” (present) | **krias** | cries / shouts | OK | | **non** | negation adverb “not” | **ne** | not | OK | | **lascia** | verb “lets / permits” (present) | **permesas** | permits | OK | | **altrui** | indefinite pronoun “any other (person)” | **al iu ajn** | to anyone else | OK | | **pasar** | infinitive “to pass” | **pasi** | to pass | OK | | **per** | preposition “through / along” (introducing *la sua via*) | **laŭ** | along / according to | OK | | **la** | definite article (feminine) – part of *la sua via* | — | (none) | **UNNECESSARY** | | **sua** | possessive adjective “its” (modifies *via*) | **ĝia** | its | OK | | **via** | noun “way / road” (object of *per*) | **vojo** | way | OK | | **ma** | coordinating conjunction “but” | **sed** | but | OK | | **tanto** | adverb of degree “so much / to such an extent” | **tiel** | so / thus | OK | | **lo** | accusative pronoun “him” (object of *'mpedisce*) | **lin** | him | OK | | **'mpedisce** | verb “hinders / impedes” (present) | **malhelpas** | hinders | OK | | **che** | complementizer introducing result clause “that” | **ke** | that | OK | | **l'uccide** | verb “kills him” (present) | **mortigas** | kills | OK |
---
### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: the Italian definite article **la** appears twice (in *la qual* and *la sua via*). Esperanto does not use articles, so they are omitted in the translation. No other tokens are missing, wrong, or grammatically problematic.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Esperanto script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Esperanto text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
